newsitem.title: FRANCE: French group has no news of kidnapped aid workers.
newsitem.headline: French group has no news of kidnapped aid workers.

text.p: A French refugee aid group said on Sunday it was concerned about four Frenchmen missing in Chechnya after getting no more news about them since hearing last week that they were in good health and being well treated.

Alain Michel, president of the Lyon-based relief group Equilibre, said there had been no contact with kidnappers who seized the four -- three Equilibre staffers and a friend -- in Russia's Dagestan republic in the north Caucasus on August 3.
"We don't have any precise news. We don't know who the kidnappers are or who to talk with to get (our colleagues) free," he told France Info radio.

A report last week from Russian sources saying the four were taken to Chechnya had not yet been confirmed by any other sources, he said, adding that Equilibre did not know if the kidnapping was politically motivated or an act of banditry.
"For the time being, we're talking with people who might know something but not with the kidnappers themselves," he said.
Equilibre said last week the Russian foreign ministry had informed it that the four men had been brought to Chechnya and were in good health.
The four had been in Dagestan, a small republic in the extreme southeastern corner of the Russian Federation, for several months to aid refugees from Chechnya.
